title: Test and Lint Ansible Content
objective: Build a layered quality pipeline using linting, syntax checks, assertions, check mode, Molecule, CI, and functional tests.

sourceAlignment.title: Ansible for DevOps, 2nd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Jeff Geerling
sourceAlignment.chapterTitle: Testing and CI for Ansible Content

paragraphs: Testing has layers. yamllint checks YAML style, ansible-playbook --syntax-check parses playbooks, and ansible-lint detects risky or non-idiomatic Ansible patterns. None proves the system works, but each gives fast feedback.

debug exposes values; assert and fail encode invariants. Check mode previews supported changes but is not a complete simulation. Molecule creates disposable instances, converges roles or playbooks, verifies outcomes, and tests idempotence.

CI runs the same checks on every change. GitHub Actions or another runner can install pinned tooling, lint, execute Molecule, and run testinfra or serverspec functional assertions against the resulting system.
explanation.rule: Order checks from fast and static to slower and realistic, and test idempotence explicitly.

examples.title: Quality Pipeline
examples.code:
pipeline:
  - yamllint
  - syntax_check
  - ansible_lint
  - molecule_test
  - functional_verify
examples.note: Fast failures come first; environment-backed verification comes last.

checks.question: What does Molecule add beyond syntax checking?

feedback.incorrect: Molecule exercises content in disposable environments.

assignment.title: Order the Quality Gates
assignment.brief: Complete the pipeline from YAML linting through functional verification.
requirements: Include all five gates in the demonstrated order.
assignment.solutionCode:
pipeline:
  - yamllint
  - syntax_check
  - ansible_lint
  - molecule_test
  - functional_verify

hints: Static checks come before environment creation.
